snapshot.source: 7 May 2026 step-9b post-audit (live vs shadow MAE per multiplier tier)
snapshot.method: per-tier multiplier left at value where live_mae < shadow_mae and live_signed_bias near zero; London tier set to 0.0 because audit showed live MAE 10.86pp vs shadow 7.43pp (uplift made London bias worse by 3.43pp)
snapshot.revision: Multipliers swept and chosen by hold-out rather than by eye (scripts/sweep-uplift-multipliers.mjs). Only metropolitan changed: every one of the five folds picked 1.00 over the hand-set 0.75, and on its own the change improves four of five folds on both metrics, worth +1.50pp of winner accuracy and -0.085pp of MAE held out. London 0.00 and northern-unitary 1.00 were confirmed by the sweep (4 of 5 folds each) and left alone. The 'other' tier is unresolved: three folds preferred 0.60 and two preferred the hand-set 0.85, and adopting every fold's preference produced one badly negative fold, so it stays at 0.85 until there is a second real election to fit on.

fitted.note: The 7 May 2026 audit evidence below is what justified 0.75 originally. It was right that the uplift helps here and wrong about how much: the tier wanted full lift.

hard_plausibility_ceiling.description: Override that caps Reform UK predicted share regardless of region multiplier. Applied AFTER the uplift step.
hard_plausibility_ceiling.rationale: 7 May post-audit found Reform predicted shares >25% in wards where actual Reform was 0-8%. Those wards all had asian_pct > 0.40 or were inner-suburb high-degree London wards. The hard ceiling forces Reform to demographic-plausibility regardless of upstream model drift.
